Opioid Treatment Program - Intake Note

Patient: 34-year-old male presenting to OTP for evaluation of ongoing heroin use, seeking to start methadone maintenance therapy. Patient states he has been using intranasal and IV heroin daily for the past 3 years, with escalating tolerance and unsuccessful attempts to quit on his own. He reports that he wants to enter maintenance treatment because he is "tired of chasing the drug" and wants to rebuild his relationship with his family.

Diagnosis: Patient meets DSM-5 criteria for Opioid Use Disorder, severe, based on interview - tolerance, withdrawal, unsuccessful efforts to cut down, craving, continued use despite social/interpersonal problems, and time spent obtaining/using the drug.

Assessment today included discussion of maintenance treatment options (methadone vs buprenorphine), and patient voluntarily elected methadone maintenance after review of risks and benefits.

Medical history reviewed: denies chronic medical conditions, prior psychiatric hospitalization x1 for depression in 2019, denies significant trauma history, hepatitis status unknown, not currently pregnant (patient is male). Physical exam performed in office - vitals stable, track marks noted on bilateral antecubital fossae, no acute distress, lungs clear, heart regular rate and rhythm, abdomen soft/non-tender.

Mental health screening completed - PHQ-9 score 8 (mild depressive symptoms), no active suicidal ideation.

Labs drawn today: CBC, LFTs, HIV, Hepatitis B/C panel, and TB skin test placed - results pending.

Informed consent for methadone maintenance treatment discussed at length, including risks of overdose, QT prolongation, interactions with other CNS depressants, and benefits of stabilization. Patient signed consent form.

Treatment plan formulated: methadone induction starting at 30mg with daily dosing, weekly counseling sessions with OTP counselor, patient expressed interest in individual therapy and declined group therapy at this time.

Withdrawal assessment: COWS score 14 (moderate withdrawal), plan for methadone induction per protocol with close monitoring over first two weeks.

Overdose/safety assessment completed - discussed risk of overdose especially if combined with other depressants, discussed fentanyl contamination risk, naloxone kit offered and patient accepted training and take-home kit.

Urine drug screen collected today, positive for opiates and negative for other substances, consistent with reported use pattern.

Patient will be followed by our OTP physician and licensed addiction counselor as part of our SAMHSA-certified opioid treatment program per federal regulations.

Plan: Begin methadone induction, await lab results, follow up in 2 days for dose adjustment and reassessment.

[Note: Portions of this intake, including specific counselor documentation and signed consent form copies, are maintained in a separate internal binder system not currently integrated with the EHR; front desk staff report some older intake records from this transition period may be difficult to locate promptly if requested for audit.]
